executiveSummary: GM0230 passes the deterministic execution contract for all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its official 2025 identity, generalized boundary, 23,903 residents, 22 neighbourhoods, three BAG places and demographic arithmetic are coherent. Six generated A28/N308/N309/N310 links were checked against all sixteen current NWB wvk_id records and their own wegnummer fields; the engine correctly limits them to Mobility and road-logistics Supply. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset assigns Elburg a persistent 2.317148 m-equivalent internal flood stress, shows 100 percent inundation stress at T+72 and raises affected population from 13,884 to 14,717 without selecting a connected Elburg, Randmeren, IJssel or primary-defence event. The official regional profile instead names specific Hackfort and Cortenoever breach scenarios, and Rijkswaterstaat warns that older Veluwerandmeer hydraulic calculations at Elburg materially overestimated levels. Eight noncompound nonzero hazard families reuse one exact 22-neighbourhood order; the compound map retains the same underlying seed with saturation ties. In a controlled fire placed inside the official Elburg6 mixed-forest polygon and Buitengebied ’t Harde Zuid, the source neighbourhood ranks last. This conflicts with 24.41 km² of documented local nature area, the A28/ASK fire history and the official short-reaction-time nature-fire mechanism. Public HWH data identifies an in-boundary Elburg RWZI, two sewer pumps, three surface-water pumps including Havensluis, two sluices and 49 weirs, but the service/recovery curves use none of their connectivity or event state. Municipal plans, provider territories, capacity samples and current observations are valuable context only: they do not prove topology, operation, damage or T+72 restoration, and NoData/no match must never become zero or safe.
provinceReviewFlags: Municipality-specific release blocker GM0230-RIVER-001: persistent critical direct inundation and a 100 percent public hero lack a selected Elburg/Randmeren/IJssel event, connected footprint, defence state or locally valid hydraulic time series.

Municipality-specific release blocker GM0230-SPATIAL-001: eight unrelated noncompound hazards share one exact 22-neighbourhood order and compound retains the same underlying seed; GM0230 has no municipality-specific unsupported-result guard.

Municipality-specific release blocker GM0230-FIRE-001: a controlled source inside the official Elburg6 mixed-forest polygon and BU02300209 ranks 22nd of 22 despite strong local A28/ASK nature-fire evidence.

Municipality-specific release blocker GM0230-PLUVIAL-001: a precise generic cloudburst rank is shown while the municipality is still producing its System Overview Urban Water and new street/neighbourhood stress test and has explicitly differentiated ’t Harde drainage works.

Municipality-specific release blocker GM0230-HEAT-DROUGHT-001: the 2025 regional climate atlas separates heat, drought, rain and flooding, but the model reuses the common rank and fixed scenario values without sampling those surfaces.

Municipality-specific release blocker GM0230-WATERCHAIN-001: exact drainage/water values omit the public RWZI, Havensluis, surface-water pumps, sewer pumps, sluices and weirs; register status is not live operation.

Municipality-specific release blocker GM0230-RECOVERY-001: river pressure/affected population and compound pressure worsen from T+24 to T+72 without a selected event, recession, asset condition, access or response-resource ledger.

Municipality-specific continuity gap: N309/Elburgerbrug, A28, ’t Harde station and external acute care are material cross-boundary dependencies, but static NWB/ProRail/GTFS and current observations do not establish scenario-time access.
Shared/national safeguard confirmed: unqualified NWB geometry supports only Mobility and road logistics/Supply and does not masquerade as power, water, drainage, gas, telecom or facilities topology.
Shared/national: replace centre-distance water fields and the common neighbourhood hash with selected hazard-specific surfaces, source containment, typed coverage and visible unsupported states.

Shared/national: official observations, registers, provider territories, planning capacity and project pages remain official context, not simulated forcing or future service state; no-data, stale, outside-boundary and no-match remain Unknown.

identity.summary: GM0230, Elburg, province Gelderland and safety region Noord- en Oost-Gelderland are internally and officially coherent.
notes: The generated feature id, bundle code/name, province, boundary/statistics edition and safety-region assignment agree.
Reference point [5.840894667389957, 52.4233858168439] lies inside the generalized 2025 municipality geometry.

The official CBS row contains padded code GM0230, 23,903 residents, density 375 residents per square kilometre, 5,073 residents aged 65 or older and 2,822 one-person households; the generated 21.2 percent age-65 share is consistent after division and rounding.
The padded official OData identifier is a source-field semantic, not an identity mismatch.

geography.summary: The municipality, 22-neighbourhood, place and settlement geometries are coherent, but administrative polygons cannot substitute for Randmeren hydraulics, urban drainage, forest fuel, service zones or incident footprints.
notes: BoundaryEdition and statisticsEdition both equal 2025; the three official BAG places are Elburg, Doornspijk and ’t Harde.
Ten BRT settlement labels comprise five woonkernen, one gehucht and four buurtschappen; they orient the map but are not population, evacuation or service zones.
Elburg spans the low Randmeren/vesting water system and the wooded Veluwe flank around ’t Harde. The official sources distinguish those mechanisms; the shared neighbourhood seed does not.
Administrative polygons, HWH point assets, provider territories, NWB sections, risk polygons, climate rasters and current observations retain separate provenance and coverage.

demography.summary: Headline population and aggregate vulnerability inputs agree with CBS 2025 and neighbourhood totals reconcile within official publication rounding.
notes: Twenty-two independently rounded neighbourhood rows sum to 23,905 residents, two above the municipality total, a +0.008 percent publication-rounding difference; they sum to 9,755 households and 5,075 residents aged 65 or older.
The model transparently reconciles neighbourhood population to the official 23,903 municipality total; this allocation is not a revision of CBS observations.

Population, age, household form, housing form, density, cars and GP/supermarket distance support aggregate vulnerability and service-demand context, but do not identify individuals, live location, medical dependence, preparedness or emergency priority.
Suppressed, incomplete, unknown and not-applicable values remain null rather than zero.

regionalDetail.summary: Twenty-two neighbourhoods provide useful social and land-use context, but partial fields and a hazard-independent allocator prevent operational prioritization.
notes: All 22 neighbourhoods carry most population, age, household, business, housing, land and water fields. Home value and multifamily fields cover 20/22; household size and GP/supermarket distance cover 21/22; cars per household covers 19/22; district-heating share and public-charging count cover 0/22 and remain null.
Largest generated neighbourhood populations are Oosthoek 2,955 before reconciliation, Vrijheid 2,440, ’t Harde West 2,405, ’t Harde Centrum 2,170, Doornspijk 1,900 and Oostendorp 1,800.
Official planning distinguishes vesting/Randmeren water controls, ’t Harde climate works and a large mixed-forest area. None is represented by the common local hazard order.
Compound T+24 local population, affected population and all eight service demand/delivery totals reconcile, but this arithmetic does not validate the spatial rank.

settlements.summary: Three BAG places and differentiated BRT settlement labels represent Elburg’s polycentric municipality without fabricating population or response zones.
notes: Elburg, Doornspijk and ’t Harde are the three in-boundary BAG woonplaats records; none of their reference centres falls outside the generalized boundary.
The ten BRT labels are ’t Harde, Aperloo, Doornspijk, Elburg, Hoge Enk, Lage Bijssel, Nieuwstad, Oostendorp, Oudekerk and Wessinge, classified as woonkern, gehucht or buurtschap.
Place centres and settlement labels are not evacuation areas, shelters, service districts, catchments or live occupancy.

transport.summary: Six logical road links and ’t Harde station have coherent current source identity and correct service scope, but static records do not establish first-72-hour access.
notes: Generated links are A28 toward Nunspeet and Oldebroek, N310 toward Nunspeet, N309 toward Dronten and Epe, and N308 toward Oldebroek, backed by sixteen distinct NWB wvk identifiers with no duplicate source id.

Every source section was re-queried from current NWB by wvk_id and checked against its own wegnummer: A28 sections report 028, the N310 pair report N310, both N309 pairs report N309 and the N308 pair report N308. This is source-field verification, not proof of passability.

The current engine includes all six links only for Mobility and Supply and includes zero NWB routes for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom or facilities. Nominal 260/150 logical capacity values are not measured road or logistics throughput.

ProRail station ’t Harde lies inside GM0230 and 17 scheduled transit stop areas are deployment context. Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS cannot prove a bridge/road open, a train/bus running, evacuation throughput, repair access or ambulance travel at T+0–72.
N309 crosses toward Dronten over the Randmeren system; RWS offers waterway, bridge/lock and current-navigation context, but the simulator has no event-valid Elburgerbrug operating state.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong public water, provider, telecom, education, planning and external-care context exists, but complete topology, incident state and response resources do not.
notes: Exact point-in-polygon intersection with deployed HWH data finds 57 in-boundary records: two sewer pumps, one Elburg wastewater treatment plant, three surface-water pumps, two sluices and 49 weirs. Havensluis, Goorpoort and Goorpomp are identifiable public context, not a connected hydraulic model or live state.

Mijn Aansluiting identifies Liander electricity/gas, Vitens drinking water and Ziggo media at the reference point; drainage returns no feature and therefore remains Unknown. Provider territories identify responsibility, not topology, capacity, coverage quality, outage or restoration.

The deployment contains 51 RDI antenna installations, 15 active DUO education-location records, seven KVK-derived government/public-safety points and no in-boundary RIVM emergency department. Nearest acute-care record is St. Jansdal Harderwijk at 17.74 km straight-line; none of these records establishes service coverage, shelter role, route, staffing or incident capacity.

One Netbeheer Nederland sample at postcode 8085PH resolves to Liander service area OS NUNSPEET 10-2i and reports 29 MW existing withdrawal, 32 MW required and 14.6 MW queued across 26 requests. It is one large-user planning sample, not complete Elburg coverage or live load/outage information.

No authorized complete feeder, drinking-water pressure-zone, sewer-catchment, gas, telecom-backhaul, care-route, pharmacy/food/fuel stock, priority-customer, crew, vehicle, generator, pump-control, backup or restoration dataset is loaded or inferred.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets execute at six required checkpoints for all eight services, but deterministic completion is not Elburg calibration.
notes: Peak municipality severities are severe storm 0.772021, pluvial 0.463284, river 0.729349, coastal 0.013312, heat 0.720040, winter 0.661719, cyber 0.437088, earthquake 0.074916, wildfire 0.183771 and compound 0.953249.

At T+72 storm, pluvial, coastal, winter, earthquake and wildfire current severity are zero; heat remains 0.112562, cyber remains 0.043709, river remains 0.729349 and compound remains 0.526415. These are preset trajectories, not observations or forecasts.

River internal flood stress remains 2.317148 at T+24 and T+72. Coastal direct flood stress is zero while T+24 wind is 16.109319 m/s; that narrow zero is not an assessment of Randmeren, IJssel, local drainage or defence failure.

Canonical wildfire has zero local direct flame at T+24 and represents transported smoke/drought; the Groningen-centred earthquake has no current shaking by T+24. These scoped zeros are not all-clears for another local source.
Every weather, flood, fire, seismic and cyber value is a deterministic exercise assumption, not an observed event, probability, warning, attack intelligence, outage or forecast.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, determinism, exact no-event behavior, cumulative burden, route limits, local reconciliation and layer invariance pass on the current snapshot.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0230 pnpm audit:model passed two focused tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 35.30 seconds, with 35.10 seconds test execution.
Every zero-intensity preset produces exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.

Repeated frames are deterministic; values are finite and bounded; cumulative person-hours are monotonic; route flow remains within effective logical capacity; all eight municipal service weights participate and sum to one.

T+24 local allocation reconciles population, affected population and all eight demand/delivery balances. Maximum observed floating-point discrepancies are 1.0658141036401503e-14 for local reconciliation, 1.4210854715202004e-14 for demand and 1.0658141036401503e-14 for delivery.
Changing among all eleven map layers leaves municipal and local hazard invariant; maximum observed local hazard delta is zero.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One shared neighbourhood seed, an unselected direct-flood field and failed forest-source containment contradict Elburg’s official water and nature-fire geography.
notes: Current local allocation seeds neighbourhood hazard without a selected hazard-specific surface or source containment. Severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire consequently share one exact 22-neighbourhood order. Compound uses the same underlying order, with ties introduced by saturation.

The shared top order begins Broeklanden, Oosthoek, Buitengebied Elburg Noord, Vrijheid, Havengebied, Oostendorp and Wildemaet-Molendorp regardless of whether the mechanism is rain, river water, heat, cyber or transported smoke.

A controlled source [5.881205806544506, 52.38574541464985] lies inside official mixed-forest polygon Elburg6 and BU02300209 Buitengebied ’t Harde Zuid. At T+24 the model creates direct fire 0.495854, smoke 0.597125 and severity 0.540833, yet the containing neighbourhood ranks last at 0.445756 while Broeklanden ranks first at 0.626194.

The regional profile records 2,441 ha/24.41 km² of Elburg nature area, an Elburg A28 forest/heath fire in 2003 and ASK heath fires in 2003 and 2018. It describes smoke affecting campgrounds, motorways and villages and short reaction times, so source containment/access cannot be replaced by a municipality hash.

GM0230 has no municipality-specific unsupported-spatial note. The browser renders precise local ranks, affected counts and service values while its global header reports unsupported municipalities, which does not disclose Elburg’s own unsupported dimensions.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances and dependency ledgers are inspectable, but exact Elburg magnitudes lack reviewed topology, asset state and continuity evidence.
notes: Current source applicability yields six Elburg NWB snapshots for Mobility and the same six for Supply, and zero for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom and facilities. This semantic safeguard is correct.

River T+24 availability is power 0.470126, water 0.447279, drainage 0.239578, gas 0.683258, telecom 0.416185, mobility 0.380440, facilities 0.545062 and supply 0.362024. At T+72 facilities falls to 0.368384 while the other seven values remain unchanged.

Compound availability worsens from T+24 to T+72: power 0.383223 to 0.373200, water 0.410515 to 0.407952, drainage 0.272078 to 0.269990, gas 0.605569 to 0.603942, telecom 0.224894 to 0.217820, mobility 0.626455 to 0.615785, facilities 0.372242 to 0.368193 and supply 0.162830 to 0.161840.

The VNOG power-outage exercise explicitly includes Elburg and supports dependency directions from power to trains, electrically operated bridges/doors, telecom, pumping/RWZI, drinking water, care and shops. It is one regional exercise, not calibration of the canonical hazard presets or proof of actual assets/backups.

The graph contains no named Liander feeder/switch, Vitens pressure area, telecom backhaul, sewer-pump/catchment/receiving-water/RWZI chain, Elburgerbrug state, hospital acceptance route, shelter, food/fuel depot or crew base. Unavailable authorized or security-sensitive topology remains Unknown.
NWB Mobility/Supply snapshots are logical transfer proxies. Their nominal capacities are scenario ceilings, not measured traffic or logistics throughput.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipal ledgers close arithmetically and expose evidence class, dependency order, operational assumptions and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; every service baseline plus exact-stage deltas sums to availability; weighted service shortfalls sum to municipal pressure.
System-pressure weights are power 0.18, water 0.15, drainage 0.08, gas 0.09, telecom 0.12, mobility 0.12, facilities 0.14 and supply 0.12, totaling one.
Dependency chains, local-context factors, drivers, recovery progress and restore-service counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.

Household preparedness affects modeled people/supply consequences rather than physical fragility. Day type, start clock, demand, backup, network and repair multipliers are normalized and labeled scenario assumptions; interventions are response-delayed and do not masquerade as actual Elburg crews/assets.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure relative to a matched no-event baseline before intermunicipal transfers and apply a preparedness multiplier. They are a modeled pre-transfer burden proxy, not observed outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.
Arithmetic explainability does not validate the common spatial seed, direct-flood field, utility topology or recovery calibration identified in the open findings.

recovery72h.summary: Recovery guards are numerically coherent, but Elburg’s sustained river and compound trajectories have no selected event, hydraulic state, access condition or response-resource evidence.
notes: Canonical river stress/severity remain 2.317148/0.729349 from T+24 through T+72. Pressure rises 0.552280 to 0.577014, affected population rises 13,884 to 14,717 and cumulative proxy person-hours rise 222,321.70 to 862,889.32 without a selected boundary, defence failure, connected footprint, arrival, duration, recession or pump state.

Compound severity falls from 0.947170 at T+24 to 0.526415 at T+72, rain and wind end and cyber disruption drops from 0.383457 to 0.049873, yet pressure rises 0.619360 to 0.624677, affected residents rise 16,143 to 16,323 and all eight services worsen.

Public registers/plans identify relevant assets and generic response mechanisms, while the VNOG selected flood exercise assumes pre-event evacuation and months-long inundation and its power exercise describes staged switching/generator recovery. None supplies event-valid Elburg crews, access, backups, priorities or restoration for these runs.

Headless Chromium at 1440×1000 selected Elburg, the river preset and T+72 and traversed all eleven layers without page, console or local HTTP errors. It displayed Scenario severity 100% inundation stress with evidence class derived-screening and no Elburg-specific unsupported warning.
Rendering and a generic evidence-class label do not validate magnitude, timing or restoration. Until a selected source/resource ledger exists, the trajectory is a non-operational sensitivity only.

findings.summary: The major-river preset presents persistent critical Elburg inundation without a selected locally connected water or defence event.
findings.evidence: E04 names Hackfort/dijkring 50 and Cortenoever/dijkring 52 as specific regional breach scenarios and says their LIWO products are retrievable; it does not select an Elburg or Randmeren footprint. E06 shows Drontermeer as a Randmeer at Elburg and reports that older PROMOVERA levels were likely about 0.75 m too high at Elburg, with time dependence and bottlenecks needing improvement. The canonical preset nevertheless holds internal flood stress 2.317148 and severity 0.729349 at T+24 and T+72, raises affected residents from 13,884 to 14,717 and displays 100 percent inundation stress without a GM0230 unsupported note.
findings.action: Before release mark Elburg river magnitude, local ranks and derivative service outputs unsupported and grey precise values unless an expert selects a versioned LIWO/Randmeren/IJssel or defence event with boundary condition, defence assumption, connected depth/arrival/duration/recession, units, resolution, licence and NoData. Keep indirect regional supply effects separate from direct local inundation and add focused/browser regressions.

findings.summary: Unrelated hazards reuse one exact Elburg neighbourhood order, so precise local ranks are not hazard-specific evidence.
findings.evidence: At T+24 severe storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire have the identical 22-neighbourhood order beginning Broeklanden, Oosthoek and Buitengebied Elburg Noord; compound retains the same underlying seed but saturation creates ties. E03, E05, E06 and E07 expose different urban-water, heat/drought, hydraulic and forest geometries. No GM0230-specific unsupported dimension is emitted.
findings.action: Replace the common seed with versioned hazard-specific surfaces and typed coverage/NoData. Until then attach a GM0230 unsupported note to all nine nonzero local hazard families, hide rank language and grey derived affected/service values rather than imply neighbourhood calibration.

findings.summary: The local fire allocator fails source containment inside Elburg’s official mixed-forest area.
findings.evidence: E07 returns source-held polygon isor_brandbaar_natuurgebied.0230060066722, Elburg6, mixed broadleaf/conifer forest. A controlled source [5.881205806544506, 52.38574541464985] is inside it and BU02300209 Buitengebied ’t Harde Zuid. At T+24 direct fire is 0.495854 and smoke 0.597125, yet the source neighbourhood ranks 22/22 at 0.445756 while Broeklanden ranks first at 0.626194. E04 documents 24.41 km² nature area, Elburg A28/ASK fires, scarce access/bluswater and short evacuation reaction time.
findings.action: Use the IPO/Risicokaart WFS as static combustible-area eligibility, then require a selected ignition/perimeter and event-valid wind, fuel moisture and access. Enforce source containment before spread, preserve polygon edition/NoData and label response resources synthetic unless the authority supplies event state.

findings.summary: The cloudburst map presents precise local allocation without the municipality’s evolving urban-water system and street-scale stress-test evidence.
findings.evidence: E03 says Elburg is preparing a 2026 System Overview Urban Water and a new stress test to identify vulnerable streets/neighbourhoods. Its ’t Harde phase 3 project explicitly adds Aquaflow, IT sewer, wadi overflow and roof disconnection for extreme-rain nuisance. At T+24 the canonical pluvial run shows flood stress 0.409428, pressure 0.294588 and 5,206 affected residents, but its rank is the same as seven unrelated hazards and does not sample these systems.
findings.action: Treat current neighbourhood pluvial ranks and service consequences as unsupported. Request versioned native municipal/regional rain-depth-duration and urban-water outputs when available, with terrain/sewer assumptions, units, resolution, validation, licence and NoData; retain project pages as context only.

findings.summary: Heat and drought use the common neighbourhood seed despite integration-ready regional surfaces and materially different water-supply context.
findings.evidence: E05’s updated 2025 regional atlas supplies downloadable planning layers for perceived temperature, warm nights, groundwater, rain and flooding; E04 identifies older residents and urban fabric as heat vulnerabilities. E05/E06 also distinguish areas with Randmeren water supply and current water state. The canonical heat run holds 26.074896°C and drought 0.625344 at T+24 and T+72 but ranks neighbourhoods identically to flood, cyber and winter weather.
findings.action: Sample versioned atlas heat and drought/groundwater surfaces separately, combine them with transparent aggregate vulnerability and keep climate scenarios distinct from timestamped KNMI/Waterinfo observations. Preserve NoData and publish units, resolution, scenario horizon and licence per layer.

findings.summary: Exact water and drainage outputs omit Elburg’s identifiable public wastewater, sluice and pumping chain.
findings.evidence: E05’s public HWH sources yield 57 in-boundary objects: two sewer pumps, Elburg RWZI, three surface-water pumps, two sluices and 49 weirs. Havensluis discharges excess stadsgracht water and keeps outside water out as part of the primary Randmeren defence; E05 also identifies a current ’t Harde–Oostendorp wastewater transport-line project. The model contains no connected catchment/receiving-water/RWZI or structure-state graph yet reports river T+24 water 0.447279 and drainage 0.239578.
findings.action: Use HWH IMWA/DAMO/GWSW and water-board exports as typed register/context overlays, not operational truth. Build an owner-reviewed or transparently synthetic catchment-to-pump/sluice/RWZI dependency graph with capacity units, backup, current state and coverage; keep absent topology Unknown and gate exact service values meanwhile.

findings.summary: Cross-boundary road, rail, bridge and acute-care continuity is material but unresolved at scenario time.
findings.evidence: E02 verifies six logical links from sixteen current NWB sections and station ’t Harde; E06 identifies the Drontermeer/Elburg crossing context. GM0230 has no in-boundary RIVM emergency department and E08 places St. Jansdal Harderwijk 17.74 km straight-line away. Static roads, station/GTFS records and bridge/waterway registers do not establish closure, timetable operation, ambulance access or throughput; the deployed NDW snapshot has zero in-boundary incidents, which means no matched current record rather than open roads.
findings.action: Add event-valid route/bridge/rail state with source and valid time where public feeds support it, route external-care accessibility over the actual network and show Unknown when unmatched. If future scenario states are synthetic, expose closure, throughput and repair assumptions rather than carrying current observations into T+72.

findings.summary: Provider and facility context is useful, but public data does not authorize exact local lifeline topology or live operating state.
findings.evidence: E08 identifies Liander power/gas, Vitens water and Ziggo media at the reference point, one OS NUNSPEET 10-2i planning sample, 51 antenna sites, 15 education locations and no in-boundary emergency department. Drainage provider lookup is empty. E04’s regional power exercise supports rapid cascades into telecom, rail, pumping, water, care and shops, with staged restoration, but it is not an actual Elburg incident or canonical-preset calibration.
findings.action: Keep provider territories, planning queues, registers and facility roles official-context/noncausal. Seek authorized aggregated service-zone, outage, backup and restoration inputs; when unavailable, use explicitly synthetic nodes/capacities with sensitivity ranges and never infer physical topology from territory geometry.

findings.summary: River and compound T+24–72 deterioration is not tied to an Elburg event, asset state, access or response-resource ledger.
findings.evidence: River pressure rises 0.552280 to 0.577014 and affected population 13,884 to 14,717 while seven service values freeze and facilities falls 0.545062 to 0.368384. Compound rain/wind end and cyber falls 0.383457 to 0.049873, yet pressure rises 0.619360 to 0.624677, affected population 16,143 to 16,323 and all eight services worsen. No selected defence/recession, Havensluis/pump/RWZI state, N309/A28/rail access, backup, crew, priority or action explains the trajectory.
findings.action: Drive recovery from a selected event plus explicit damaged assets, access, dependencies, response delay, repair tasks/resources and uncertainty. Keep intervention effects delayed/bounded and label them assumptions; until calibrated, show trajectories as non-operational sensitivities and test monotonic causal consistency when forcing declines.

findings.summary: The remaining presets are bounded exercises whose local magnitude and scope must not be mistaken for observations or all-clear statements.
findings.evidence: E04 supports regional severe rain/wind, long heat/drought, nature fire, cyber and lifeline cascades, but says the region is not expected to experience building-damaging earthquakes and separately identifies historic dense-centre fire in Elburg. Canonical earthquake current shaking is zero by T+24, coastal direct flood stress is zero, and wildfire has no local flame; those scoped zeros do not evaluate another source. KNMI, Waterinfo, air, seismic and NDW coverage is sparse and timestamped.
findings.action: Keep storm, winter and cyber amplitudes explicitly synthetic until scenario data is selected; retain coastal/earthquake/wildfire zeros as scoped no-effect outputs, not safety claims. Label historic-centre fire as outside the current natural-disaster preset scope rather than conflating it with wildfire.

findings.summary: The deterministic model, accounting, logical-road applicability and eleven-layer browser contract pass for Elburg.
findings.evidence: The focused 10×6×8 gate passes; all local population/demand/delivery balances reconcile within 1.4210854715202004e-14; layer changes alter no hazard value; all sixteen NWB source ids are unique and verified by current wvk_id/wegnummer; NWB supports only Mobility and Supply. Chromium selected Elburg/river/T+72 and traversed all eleven layers with zero page, console or local HTTP errors.
findings.action: Preserve these invariants and add regressions for GM0230 unsupported states, selected-event provenance, forest source containment, NoData display and event-valid recovery when the open corrections are implemented.

corrections.summary: Add a GM0230 unsupported guard and withhold the unselected 2.317148 direct-flood magnitude and derivative precision.
corrections.validation: Smallest safe correction: emit explicit GM0230 unsupported dimensions for all nine nonzero local hazard families, suppress/grey precise major-river magnitude, ranks, affected and derivative services, and keep direct inundation separate from indirect supply sensitivity. Durable integration requires a versioned selected LIWO/Randmeren/IJssel/defence event. Run unit, focused GM0230, national ALL and browser evidence-state tests.

corrections.summary: Replace the common neighbourhood seed with hazard-specific Elburg surfaces and enforce local fire source containment.
corrections.validation: Integrate the 2025 Vallei en Veluwe climate-atlas products and IPO combustible-nature polygons with per-layer edition, event/scenario semantics, units, resolution, licence, coverage and NoData. Require selected ignition/perimeter and containment before fire spread. Assert unrelated hazards do not share one exact rank and the controlled Elburg6 source neighbourhood no longer ranks last.

corrections.summary: Represent Elburg’s water, provider, continuity and facility records as typed context and owner-reviewed or explicitly synthetic dependencies.
corrections.validation: Retain HWH/WWV assets, Liander/Vitens/Ziggo territories, NBNL planning sample, RDI/DUO/RIVM and NWB/ProRail as noncausal official context. Add provenance-aware dependency nodes only with authorized connectivity/capacity/state; otherwise use labelled synthetic fallback and Unknown. Test empty drainage/no incident/no municipal station as no-data, not zero/safe.

corrections.summary: Tie Elburg T+0–72 recovery to selected event progression and an inspectable response-resource/action ledger.
corrections.validation: Require selected hydraulic recession/persistence, asset damage, route access, backup and delayed resource/action assumptions for restoration. Verify every T+24–72 change has a causal ledger entry, intervention effects remain time-gated/bounded and the UI identifies assumptions rather than actual Elburg crews or operator estimates.

evidenceSources.title: Gemeente and buurt gegeneraliseerd 2025 with BAG, BRT TOP10NL, NWB and railway context
evidenceSources.edition: CBS/BAG 2025; current deployed BRT/NWB/ProRail snapshots inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The application consumes annual CC BY 4.0 municipality and 22-neighbourhood generalized geometries. Reference point [5.840894667389957, 52.4233858168439] lies inside GM0230; administrative, neighbourhood, place, route, water and incident geometries remain distinct.

BAG woonplaats access is https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/bag/ogc/v2/collections/woonplaats under Public Domain Mark 1.0. BRT TOP10NL access is https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/brt-top10nl/ogc/v1, national 1:10,000 topography published annually under CC BY 4.0. Three BAG places and ten BRT labels are context, not response zones.

NWB OGC API https://api.pdok.nl/rws/nationaal-wegenbestand-wegen/ogc/v1 provides national monthly CC0 road geometry. Sixteen distinct source sections support six generated logical links: A28 to Nunspeet/Oldebroek, N310 to Nunspeet, N309 to Dronten/Epe and N308 to Oldebroek; no source id is duplicated.

Live section-level queries confirm wvk_id 369375022/370377007/600142257/600144509/379383005/380384005/600144525/600144526 each reports wegnummer 028; 366380003/365379008 report N310; 600982005/601005664/381377003/381377004 report N309; and 376389005/375389028 report N308. Route labels are coherent with each section’s physical road field.

The model uses those verified NWB links only for Mobility and road logistics/Supply. Static road geometry and nominal logical capacity do not prove passability, measured throughput, evacuation capacity or repair access.
ProRail station ’t Harde lies inside GM0230 and scheduled GTFS contributes 17 stop-area records. Presence of static records does not establish scenario-time rail or bus operation.

evidenceSources.title: Meerjarenprogrammabegroting 2026–2029 and ’t Harde phase 3 climate adaptation
evidenceSources.edition: Programme budget 2026; project page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The 2026 budget states that a System Overview Urban Water will describe broader system function, bottlenecks and water-quality/quantity measures, and a new stress test will map water-nuisance-vulnerable streets/neighbourhoods.

The integration path is to obtain the native owner-authorized System Overview/stress-test outputs when released. The budget is an annual planning PDF with no operational API and no explicit standalone licence for underlying rasters; it is not current hydraulic state.

The current project page https://www.elburg.nl/Wonen_en_verhuizen/Werkzaamheden_in_uw_buurt/Herinrichting_t_Harde_fase_3 identifies an extreme-rain adaptation area using Aquaflow storage/infiltration, IT sewer, wadi overflow and roof disconnection. Expected construction starts late 2027/early 2028.

Project geometry/PDFs can inform dated asset/change context but not prove completion, citywide hazard depth, connectivity or live operation. Preserve planned/under-construction/operational state explicitly.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 and annex scenario book
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk profile 2025–2028 and March 2025 annex publication
supports: The profile recognizes IJssel/Randmeren flood risk, extensive Veluwe forest/heath, extreme rain/wind, long heat/drought, power/drinking-water/telecom disruption and cyber cascades. It says the region is not expected to experience earthquakes causing personal or building damage.

The annex https://www.vnog.nl/sites/default/files/2025-03/Regionaal-risicoprofiel_2025-2028_bijlagenboek.pdf selects Hackfort/dijkring 50 and Cortenoever/dijkring 52 and says both LIWO scenarios are retrievable. Its Hackfort example assumes 72-hour pre-evacuation, 0.5–1 m water and 1–6 months duration; it does not select an Elburg footprint.

The annex records 2,441 ha/24.41 km² nature area for Elburg, the Elburg A28 forest/heath fire in 2003 and ASK heath fires in 2003/2018. Its reference nature fire covers 1.5–2.5 km² with 5.5–6.5 km² smoke affecting campgrounds, motorway and villages, and emphasizes access/bluswater/short reaction time.

It separately describes Elburg as a dense historic centre with attached narrow/deep old buildings. That structural-fire scenario is outside the natural-disaster presets and must not be inferred from wildfire.

The power-outage exercise explicitly includes Elburg within five minutes of a Harderwijk station fire, then describes train/bridge/telecom disruption, pump/RWZI and water/care/shop impacts through four and 24 hours, most restoration after eight hours and full rebuild after 48 hours. This supports dependency directions, not actual operator state or canonical-preset calibration.

These statutory planning PDFs have no operational API/fixed cadence and no explicit standard reuse licence on publication. They structure exercises; they are not forecasts, probabilities, current incidents or local topology.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Vallei en Veluwe / HWH / Vallei en Veluwe Klimaatbestendig
evidenceSources.title: Open geodata, water-chain register and 2025 regional climate-effect atlas
evidenceSources.edition: Public registers and 2025 climate-atlas update inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The water board explicitly offers downloads and WFS through its open geodata portal and downloadable source data through its climate atlas; the ArcGIS collection https://storymaps.arcgis.com/collections/4298a7734ce64fdfb1bd08921a49cf26 was modified 10 June 2025 but declares no blanket licence, so each embedded layer’s terms must be resolved.

The 2025 impact analysis https://klimaatvalleienveluwe.nl/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/251029-Impactanalyse-klimaatverandering.pdf says the atlas was updated in 2025 and maps perceived temperature/warm nights, groundwater/drought, water on streets and flooding. These are planning/scenario layers, not current observations or T+72 forecasts.

HWH IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/ogc/v2 and DAMO https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 are national OGC APIs under CC BY-SA 4.0; GWSW https://api.pdok.nl/rioned/waterschappen-waterketen-gwsw/ogc/v1 is CC0. Contributions/completeness vary and no single fixed cadence is stated.

Exact point-in-polygon intersection finds 57 records: two sewer pumps, one Elburg RWZI, three surface-water pumps, two sluices and 49 weirs. Status realised and a registered capacity never prove connectivity, compatible units, telemetry or live operation.

The water-board page https://www.vallei-veluwe.nl/wat-doen-wij/werken-aan-schoon-water/rioolwater-zuiveren/ confirms Elburg is one of sixteen RWZI sites; the 340 million litre/day figure is the total across all sites and must not be assigned to Elburg.

The Havensluis description https://www.vallei-veluwe.nl/publish/pages/22676/fietsroute_elburg.pdf says it discharges excess stadsgracht water, keeps outside water out and is part of the primary Randmeren defence. It is static educational context, not current gate/pump state.

The project page https://www.vallei-veluwe.nl/actueel/projecten/relining-renoveren-van-leidingen/ identifies the ’t Harde–Oostendorp wastewater transport line. Its project state/cadence is not a live outage feed and does not expose full connectivity.

evidenceSources.title: Drontermeer, Waterinfo, LIWO and Veluwerandmeer hydraulic evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current RWS pages and deployed observation snapshot inspected 3 September 2026; hydraulic report dated 19 April 2021
supports: RWS identifies Drontermeer as a 10 km long, 0.2–1 km wide, shallow Randmeer between Kampen and Elburg and links current water levels, navigation notices and bridge/lock operating times. These feeds retain their own valid time and do not by themselves define road access or future availability.

RWS Waterinfo https://waterinfo.rws.nl/api/point/latestmeasurement?parameterId=waterhoogte is generally ten-minute, five-minute-cached, CC0 and non-mission-critical. The nearest deployment record is Elburg Elburgerbrug at 4.12 km from the municipal reference point, -6 cm NAP at 2026-09-02T17:30:00Z; its polygon assignment is null/outside, which is geometry semantics rather than absence of local water context.

LIWO/IPLO information is at https://iplo.nl/thema/water/applicaties-modellen/berichtgeving-crisismanagement/liwo/ and public OGC access at https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows. Layers are expert scenarios with irregular release and layer-specific licence/NoData, not one universal real-time flood surface. An adapter must require explicit scenario selection and connected footprint.

RWS analysis https://open.rijkswaterstaat.nl/@244743/analyse-hydraulische-belastingen-veluwe/ reports that older PROMOVERA estimates likely overstated normal-storm levels by 40–80 cm and norm levels at Elburg by roughly 0.75 m, and calls for improved time dependence and bottleneck treatment. It expressly warns against recycling old results without caution.

Public water, navigation and hydraulic data can support event selection/current context, but observation time, vertical datum, quality, event boundary, defence assumption, units, resolution, coverage and NoData must remain visible.

evidenceSources.title: Landelijk Informatiepunt Natuurbranden — public combustible-nature WFS
evidenceSources.edition: Metadata updated 19 February 2026; Elburg feature begin-validity 24 May 2006
supports: Integration-ready WFS/WMS access is https://servicespub.risicokaart.nl/geoserver/ISOR_RK/wfs under Public Domain catalogue terms. A live bounding-box query returns Elburg-source-held feature isor_brandbaar_natuurgebied.0230060066722, name Elburg6, classified mixed broadleaf/conifer forest.
The official polygon contains controlled source [5.881205806544506, 52.38574541464985] and BU02300209 Buitengebied ’t Harde Zuid.

The feature has begin-validity 24 May 2006, null end-validity and no guaranteed operational refresh cadence or feature-scale accuracy. It is static eligibility/planning context, not live fuel, moisture, ignition, perimeter, smoke, suppression, access or current incident.

A fire adapter must preserve polygon edition/coverage and NoData, then combine a selected source/perimeter with event-valid wind/fuel moisture and authorized access, extinguishing-water and response assumptions.

evidenceSources.publisher: Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM / KNMI / NDW
evidenceSources.title: Integration-ready public provider, capacity, telecom, facility and valid-time observation context for Elburg
evidenceSources.edition: Live provider lookup 3 September 2026; deployed public-context snapshots retrieved 2 September 2026; source editions and valid times retained
supports: Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting WMS/WFS identifies Liander power/gas, Vitens drinking water and Ziggo media at the reference point; drainage is empty and remains Unknown. Provider records were last updated 24 March 2026 for electricity, 17 December 2025 for gas and 7 September 2025 for water/media. Territories are not topology, capacity, outage or restoration.

Netbeheer Nederland capacity-map pages https://www.netbeheernederland.nl/netcapaciteit-en-flexibiliteit/capaciteitskaart describe open planning data: capacity/projects at least quarterly and queues monthly. One postcode 8085PH sample resolves to OS NUNSPEET 10-2i/Liander with 29 MW existing withdrawal, 32 MW required, 14.6 MW queued/26 requests and TenneT class 3. One point is not full municipal coverage; exact standard licence/API stability was not established.

RDI WFS https://antenneregister.nl/mapserver/wfs/ contributes 51 in-boundary antenna-site records: 22 mobile, 15 fixed link, two broadcast, one other mobile and eleven amateur. No standard licence/fixed cadence was stated. A registered site does not prove radio coverage, ownership, backhaul, power/backup, traffic, outage or restoration.

DUO RIO https://onderwijsdata.duo.nl/dataset/c416acd1-e083-4ec6-9203-3b20f98fe143 contributes 15 current registered education-location records, updates daily around 06:15 and uses Creative Commons Attribution with version unspecified. Registration does not prove occupancy, shelter designation, accessibility, staffing, supplies or backup.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 https://datacatalogus.rivm.nl/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.21945/8E767B2D-9CED-4A85-A95D-3AC1A608C663 is CC0, published 3 July 2026, and has no in-boundary emergency department; nearest is St. Jansdal Harderwijk at 17.74 km straight-line. This signals possible external dependency, not route, acceptance or live capacity.

KNMI Data Platform https://developer.dataplatform.knmi.nl/ provides product-specific valid-time weather/forecast data, commonly CC BY 4.0, with radar products around five-minute cadence. KNMI FDSN https://rdsa.knmi.nl/fdsnws/event/1 is automatically updated and defaults to CC BY 4.0. The deployment assigns zero weather stations and zero 365-day seismic origins to GM0230; nearest weather station is Lelystad Airport 22.73 km away. Sparse/no-match coverage is not zero hazard.

NDW DATEX II https://opendata.ndw.nu/actueel_beeld.xml.gz is CC0 current-picture data. The deployed snapshot has zero in-boundary GM0230 event points; no match means no matched record at that feed/valid time, never that every road or bridge is open. Current observations cannot define arbitrary scenario T+72.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic planning-model audit, not validation against an observed Elburg disaster, outage, evacuation, casualty, health, welfare or restoration dataset.
CBS and PDOK publish generalized annual administrative/statistical context; rounding, suppression, BAG/municipality geometry and timing differences remain normal source semantics.
The audit did not obtain authorized live Liander/Vitens/Ziggo, municipal sewer, fire-response, care, retail, fuel, logistics, bridge-control or priority-customer topology/state.
HWH and provider/facility registers are partial and heterogeneous; registered status or territory never proves connected topology, capacity, operation, backup, damage or restoration.
LIWO, regional climate-atlas and nature-fire products require layer/event selection, licence, edition, units, resolution, quality, coverage and NoData review before causal ingestion.
A current Waterinfo, KNMI, NDW or other observation is context for its valid time and location only; it is not a continuous surface, arbitrary scenario input or T+72 forecast.
NWB Mobility/Supply transfers remain logical proxies, not physical utility routes or measured traffic/logistics capacity; ProRail/GTFS identity does not establish service operation.

The regional risk profile is authoritative planning evidence for mechanisms and exercise structure, but not a probability forecast, live incident, complete local asset list or operator restoration estimate.

The official Elburg6 polygon identifies combustible nature, not current fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, smoke, suppression or access; the controlled source test is a falsification diagnostic, not a real incident.
Historic dense-centre fire, disease and other VNOG risks fall outside the ten canonical natural-disaster/cyber presets and must be labelled as scope gaps rather than silently represented.
NoData, suppressed values, empty queries, no in-boundary facility/station and outside-boundary observations remain Unknown or not-applicable, never zero, safe, open or operational.
